title: the ... (names of places)
subtitle: France / the Netherlands / the Nile
summary: Learn when a name of a place takes the (rivers, seas, plural names, hotels, museums) and when it takes nothing (countries, towns, streets, stations).

lesson.heading: Countries, towns and continents
lesson.text: In general we do **not** use *the* with names of continents, countries, states, islands and towns.

examples.text: **Corsica** is an island in the Mediterranean.

lesson.note: But we use **the** in names with *republic*, *states* or *kingdom*: **the** Czech Republic, **the** United States of America (**the** USA), **the** United Kingdom (**the** UK).

lesson.heading: the -s (plural names)
lesson.text: We use **the** with plural names of countries, islands and mountains.

lesson.heading: Seas, rivers and canals
lesson.text: We use **the** with names of oceans, seas, rivers and canals.

lesson.heading: Places in towns
rows: the Regent Hotel, the Park Hotel
the Science Museum, the National Gallery
lesson.note: Streets, squares, airports, stations and many important buildings take no *the*. But most hotels, museums, theatres and cinemas take **the**.

lesson.heading: the ... of ... and the north / the south
lesson.text: We always use **the** with names that have *... of ...*, and with **the north / the south / the east / the west**.

examples.text: I've been to **the north of Italy**, but not to **the south**.

lesson.text: One name can go both ways: *Cambridge University* has no *the*, but *the University of Cambridge* does, because of *of*.

exercises.prompt: ___ is the largest continent in the world.
exercises.explanation: No the with the name of a continent.
No the with the name of a town or city.

exercises.prompt: ___ is a river in South America.
exercises.explanation: Rivers always take the: the Amazon, the Nile, the Rhine.

exercises.prompt: Match each description with the right name.

pairs.left: is between Saudi Arabia and Africa
is a country in northern Europe
is an island in the Caribbean
is a country in East Africa

exercises.explanation: Plural names of countries and islands take the.

exercises.prompt: Which of these names take the?

exercises.explanation: Names of streets take no the.

exercises.statement: We went to see a play at National Theatre.
exercises.explanation: We went to see a play at the National Theatre. Theatres, cinemas, hotels and museums take the.

exercises.prompt: Have you ever been to ___ of France?
exercises.explanation: We always say the north / the south / the east / the west of a place.

exercises.statement: I hope to go to United States next year.
exercises.explanation: I hope to go to the United States next year. Names with states, republic or kingdom take the.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
exercises.answer: The Panama Canal joins the Atlantic Ocean and the Pacific Ocean.
exercises.explanation: Canals and oceans all take the.
